words.note: Select nominal 60 Hz through the existing initialization setter when the player chooses the 60 fps mode.
Keep the selected nominal 60 Hz rate when the game reads its saved frame-rate setting.
Stores the observed scene delay as negative fractional 30 Hz units; zero still selects the original immediate path.
A nonnegative fractional scene counter has expired; testing its sign also recognizes exact zero without a separate compare.
Loads the exact scale 30 times 2^16 for the scene countdown, making fractional updates independent of rendering frequency.
Transfers the exact fixed-point time scale to a caller-saved floating-point register.
Uses the game's simulation delta, already capped at 50 ms per callback; hitches keep that cap rather than catching up full wall time.
Rounds fractional units up. Non-steady or non-standard cadence may shift expiry by at most one callback; steady 30 Hz keeps the original count.
Advances the negative scene counter toward zero by elapsed simulation time instead of one whole frame per callback.
Stores the fractional scene counter in its existing word; the allocation and other state fields are unchanged.
Returns through the existing shared epilogue. Expiry is checked on the next callback, retaining frequency-dependent callback latency.
Use original 30 Hz duration units for the standard fade coefficient; preserve the existing zero-duration path.
Use original 30 Hz duration units when the standard opposite-direction fade is initialized; animation durations retain their existing seconds conversion.
Advance fades with capped elapsed time. Hitch progress differs from frame counting; very large unsigned durations can stall float progress.
Advance the opposite-direction standard fade by capped elapsed time; preserve alpha clamping and completion handling.
Keep the selected 60 Hz mode when an individual frame-rate option is applied.
Keep the selected 60 Hz mode when a graphics preset applies its frame-rate table entry.
